title: One-on-One Trading Coach
seoTitle: One-on-One Trading Coach: What to Expect
seoDescription: What one-on-one trading coaching involves, how sessions are structured, who it suits, and how it compares with group programs and self-paced courses.
headline: What One-on-One Trading Coaching Actually Involves
subheadline: Private coaching is the most expensive way to learn and the fastest, for one reason: the feedback is about you. Here is how sessions run, who benefits, and who should wait.
intro: One-on-one trading coaching means a coach reviews your actual trades, your journal, and your decisions, then corrects the specific errors you keep repeating. A typical session runs 45 to 60 minutes, covers your recent trades in detail, and ends with one or two concrete changes to apply that week. It suits traders who already have screen time and are stuck on execution rather than knowledge.

keyPoints.title: How a Session Is Structured
keyPoints.text: Most of the hour goes to your recent trades: what you saw, why you entered, what you did as it moved. The coach is looking for the gap between your stated rules and your actual behaviour, because that gap is where consistent traders and inconsistent ones separate. Sessions end with one or two specific changes, not a lecture.

keyPoints.title: What You Need to Bring
keyPoints.text: A journal with real entries, screenshots of your trades, and honesty about the ones that went wrong. Coaching works on evidence. Turning up without a record means the hour gets spent on general theory you could have watched free, which is the most common way traders waste their own money here.

keyPoints.title: One-on-One Compared With Group and Courses
keyPoints.text: Courses teach a method cheaply and are the right starting point when you are new. Group coaching adds structure and accountability at a moderate price. One-on-one costs the most and is the only format where the feedback is about your specific errors. Each is correct at a different stage, and paying for the third when you need the first wastes money.

keyPoints.title: Who Should Wait
keyPoints.text: If you have not traded a consistent method for a few months, there is nothing yet to correct and a course will serve you better. If the fee would come out of trading capital or money you need, wait. Private coaching accelerates an existing process rather than replacing the screen time that builds one.

keyPoints.title: What Progress Looks Like
keyPoints.text: Early on, fewer rule breaks rather than more profit. Then smaller losses, because the bad trades get cut sooner. Profit consistency comes later and lags the behavioural change by weeks. If you are measuring only the account balance in month one, you will conclude it is not working while it is working.

faqs.q: How long is a one-on-one trading coaching session?
faqs.a: Usually 45 to 60 minutes. R2F runs one session a week on the Lite plan and two a week on Pro and the Full Mentorship, because a second session in the same week catches errors while they are still fresh.

faqs.q: How many sessions do I need?
faqs.a: Plan for at least a quarter. The correction loop needs repetition: spot the error, apply the fix, trade the week, review again. One or two sessions can fix a specific problem but will not change how you trade.

faqs.q: Is one-on-one coaching better than a course?
faqs.a: For a trader with screen time who keeps breaking their own rules, yes, because a course cannot see what you are doing. For someone still learning the method, a course is better and far cheaper. Match the format to the stage you are at.

faqs.q: What happens in the first session?
faqs.a: Usually a review of how you currently trade: your method, your risk, and your recent results. The point is to find the one or two errors costing you the most, rather than rebuilding everything at once.

faqs.q: Do I need to already be profitable?
faqs.a: No. Most traders come in inconsistent or losing. What you do need is a method you have actually traded and a record of the trades, otherwise there is no evidence to work from.
